newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk Sabanci to sell more shares abroad.
newsitem.headline: Turk Sabanci to sell more shares abroad.

text.p: Sabanci Holding , one of Turkey's leading industrial conglomerates, said it would sell 750 million additional shares abroad after it floated five billion shares last week.

"Sabanci Holding partners...have agreed with Morgan Stanley Dean Witter which managed the foreign offer (last week), to sell 750 million additional shares, equal to 15 percent of the initial flotation to investors abroad at 3.6 cents per share within 30 days from the listing on the Istanbul Stock Exchange," the Holding said in a statement.

Sabanci Holding's publicly-owned shares began to be traded on the Exchange on Tuesday after it floated five trillion lira ($33.3 million) of new shares, or 10 percent of its capital on July 2-3 at 5,400 lira per 1,000 lira nominal valued share.

The company's share offers met heavy oversubscription both in Turkey and abroad. 4.5 trillion lira, or 90 percent of the offer was sold to 95 institutions based abroad, 450 billion lira of it to 112,182 domestic individual investors and 50 billion lira to 67 domestic institutions.
Ak securities owned by Sabanci Holding's banking arm Akbank said the additional sale of 750 million shares would be recorded on the Exchange's wholesale market on July 17.
Sabanci shares traded at 5,800 lira on the national market on Thursday, compared to 5,900 lira at Wednesday's close.
